question: Do the 2022 Eagle Cement EPRMP and 2023 SNMC EPRMP represent independent fish evidence for Conlong and Salapangan rivers?

sourceReports.citation: Eagle Cement Corporation. (2022). Environmental Performance Report and Management Plan: Eagle Cement Expansion Project – Line 4 and Additional Quarry Areas. Prepared by LCI Envi Corporation. DENR-EMB EIA document repository.
sourceReports.access: Official EMB-indexed PDF text reviewed for the project title and freshwater ecology methods, date, station table, observations, and interview leads. Direct PDF retrieval returned HTTP 403; no local copy or page image was retained.

sourceReports.citation: Solid North Mineral Corporation. (2023). Environmental Performance Report and Management Plan: SNMC Quarry Expansion Project, San Ildefonso and Doña Remedios Trinidad, Bulacan. Prepared by LCI Envi Corporation. DENR-EMB EIA document repository.
sourceReports.access: The already-reviewed official EMB-indexed PDF text was compared for the same freshwater ecology date, four station rows, fish observations, and interview leads. Direct PDF retrieval returned HTTP 403; no local copy or page image was retained.

comparison.assessmentWindow: Both reports identify the same May 7–8, 2022 freshwater ecology assessment.
observationTextMatches: Both reports name Poecilia reticulata (guppies) as visually observed at W02, W03, and W04, and both state these fish were not sampled.
Both reports describe one observed tilapia at W03 without identifying it to species.
Both reports list bulig and hito as fish reported by interviewed local fishers, not as station-linked captures.
comparison.materialOverlap: The two reports repeat the same assessment window, four station names, river/reach assignments, coordinate strings, station descriptions, and fish observation/interview statements. They therefore document overlapping source material and are not independent corroboration of these observations.
comparison.lineageInterpretation: A shared May 2022 field campaign or reuse of one underlying assessment dataset is the best-supported explanation for the matching date, full station matrix, descriptions, and observation statements. The indexed report text alone does not prove which report is the originating record, whether any additional field visit occurred, or whether the data were copied between project submissions.

evidenceLimits.fishEvidenceMode: The named guppies and one unidentified tilapia are uncollected visual observations as reported. The other names are interview leads. No voucher, specimen, observation photo, fish-specific field log, or independent identification record was verified.
evidenceLimits.datePrecision: May 7–8, 2022 is the overall freshwater assessment window, not an observation-specific date for each fish or station.
evidenceLimits.coordinateUse: Coordinates belong to the report's ecological assessment stations. They do not establish a publicly accessible fishing point, safe location, legal boundary, or independent fish specimen coordinate.
evidenceLimits.taxonomicLimit: Poecilia reticulata is the report's name for the observed guppies; the source does not provide a voucher or diagnostic basis. The W03 tilapia remains unidentified. Bulig and hito remain vernacular interview labels.
evidenceLimits.reuseLimit: No item-specific open reuse license or permission to redistribute the EPRMP-derived observations, table, map, or coordinates was verified.

decision: Register the 2022 Eagle EPRMP as an overlapping report of the already-reviewed May 2022 Conlong/Salapangan assessment. Count the matched fish statements as one research evidence unit, not two independent confirmations. Retain the existing unvouchered Poecilia visual-observation candidate and unidentified W03 tilapia as research-only; keep interview labels unassigned.
nextActions: Keep both EPRMP records linked to one May 2022 assessment lineage unless field logs establish distinct visits or independent fish observations.
Seek field sheets, dated observation photos, vouchers, or a lawful full-text copy before proposing a public species occurrence.
Do not derive current presence, catchability, safety, legal access, or a complete fish list from these reports.

sources.supports: Official EMB-indexed text for the Eagle Cement project identity, May 2022 survey window, W01–W04 station table, coordinate/reach assignments, observation statements, and interview-derived fish names.
Official EMB-indexed text for the matching SNMC May 2022 assessment date, station table, descriptions, fish observations, and interview leads.
